ART-COVER-002.identity: The Recommended First Party of Heraldry Skirmish (Human Fighter, Elf Ranger, Dwarf Cleric, Halfling Rogue), four Heroes on an expedition into the monster-haunted ruins of the Dying Lands while a rival party works the same ground.
ART-COVER-002.composition: Low three-quarter view from ground level; the four-Hero party is small in the lower third, advancing between rain-slick flagstones. A broken shrine arch frames the scene on one side and the upper half of the picture is open ruled sky, left empty for the typeset title.
details: Broken gothic shrine arch with a missing keystone and a headless saint in a wall niche
Rain drawn as sparse fine diagonal strokes, puddles on the flagstones reflecting the arch

Human Fighter in a ring shirt with shortsword and small round targe at the front, Elf Ranger in a leather coat with a shortbow, broad Dwarf Cleric in a ring shirt with a mace and small round targe, small Halfling Rogue in a leather coat with a rapier at the hip slipping along the wall edge
A rival party's tattered banner on a pole planted across the rubble, no readable device
Fallen columns, toppled statue fragments and moss on the stones
Treeline at the far edge with one Monster silhouette standing between the trunks, shape only
Lantern hung on the Ranger's pack, soaked cloaks, packs and bedrolls
activity: The four Heroes advance in a loose staggered file, weapons half-drawn, looking toward the banner
Halfling Rogue crouches at the edge peering at the banner pole
Monster silhouette stands motionless in the trees, unseen by the party
ART-COVER-002.atmosphere: Wary, rain-heavy and austere; adventurers small against withered grandeur.
avoid: Do not render the title or any lettering on banners
Do not detail the Monster: a dark silhouette only
Do not make the party large or heroic-posed; no sunburst or glow
Do not give the rival banner a heraldic device that reads as a symbol
No plate armour, longbow or staff on the four Heroes

ART-CH01-002.identity: The Dying Lands as a whole, seen from a broken mountain pass: forest on one flank, frozen peaks on the other, and the dead empire's ruined cities sprawled on the eastern horizon.
ART-CH01-002.composition: Wide vista from a high pass; a cracked imperial road winds down from the lower foreground toward the skeletal towers of a dead city on the horizon. A small party with a banner pauses at lower left, road leading the eye to the city.
details: Straight, patient imperial road paved in broken slabs, with weeds and a leaning milestone half-swallowed by roots
Forest mass pressing in on one side, drawn as dense stippled and hatched canopy
Frozen peaks with fine sparse snow-line hatching on the other side
Distant dead city of snapped spires, collapsed domes and empty arches in thin fine lines
Fractured pass rocks and a cairn in the foreground
Wisps of smoke or ash thinly ruled over the far city
Sparse horizontal cloud strokes
activity: Party of four stands on the road at lower left, one holding a banner on a pole, looking down toward the city
No other figures
ART-CH01-002.atmosphere: Vast, hushed and fatalistic; the world laid out like a wound.
avoid: Do not repeat the cover composition or the Greythorn bastion portrait; no walled town visible
No large heroic party and no legible device on the banner
Do not include any monsters or dragons in the sky
No panorama of all six climates

ART-CH02-002.identity: Two rival adventuring parties of the Dying Lands meeting in a monster-haunted ruin, each fighting for the same objective in a PvPvE skirmish.
ART-CH02-002.composition: Wide shot of a fog-filled valley of ruined walls at first light. One party crouches behind cover at lower left, the second is small at far right, a horizontal fog band crosses the middle and a monster silhouette moves in the mist between them.
details: Low ruined walls, broken arches and collapsed cottages half-lost in fog
Fog shown by sparse fine horizontal lines and blank paper
First light as a few long shadows falling lower right
Left party behind a toppled wall section, shields and a crossbow barrel just visible
Right party behind a standing gable end, a banner pole barely visible
Monster as a large dark silhouette half-dissolved in the mist, ambiguous shape
Dead tree and a broken cart wheel for scale
activity: Each party of four crouches or kneels behind cover with weapons ready, watching the other
Monster slouches through the fog between them, neither party engaging it yet
avoid: Do not show combat actually happening; this is the moment of sighting
Do not detail the Monster: a silhouette only, not a portrait
Do not repeat the cover or a bridge melee: no rain, no shrine arch, no stone bridge
No gore

ART-CH03-002.identity: The turn structure of Heraldry Skirmish, the start of a new round of activations, imagined as the dawn of a new round in the field.
ART-CH03-002.composition: Wide shot with a low horizon; a weary party gathers behind a ruined wall at left and middle ground, while a lone chapel bell tower stands as a silhouette at right over a drowned field.
details: Chapel bell tower with a cracked belfry and a rope-less bell, no cross or legible mark
Drowned field with standing water reflecting thin sky, fence posts and a half-sunken plough
Ruined wall with a broken top and fallen coping stones
Faint horizon glow suggested by blank paper above and sparse ruled strokes
Reeds and dead stalks stippled across the water
Party gear: bedrolls, shields stacked on the wall, a shared flask
A single crow on the wall top
activity: Four tired Heroes rise and stir behind the wall, one buckling armour, one tending a bandage, one scanning ahead, one asleep sitting up
All small, back or three-quarter view
ART-CH03-002.atmosphere: Weary vigilance in the first grey light.
avoid: Do not show the Heroes heroically posed; they are exhausted
No Bastion-scale bell tower: a rural chapel only
No glowing sun disk or rays
No monster in view

ART-CH04-002.identity: The movement chapter of Heraldry Skirmish, imagined as an expedition crossing a ruined imperial aqueduct over a gorge.
ART-CH04-002.composition: A strong diagonal of a broken aqueduct across the frame, deep gorge falling away beneath. Figures are caught mid-motion on different spans, with the drop dominating the lower half.
details: Roman-like arched aqueduct with collapsed spans, exposed rubble core and broken parapets
Ivy and roots hanging from the arches
Gorge floor far below drawn in fine light lines, a thread of river
Rope tied off to an arch pier and hanging into a gap
Loose stones falling from a crumbling edge
Wind-bent dead trees on the gorge rim
Packs and a lantern slung on climbers
activity: One Hero climbs a rope up a broken span
One Hero leaps a gap between spans, cloak streaming
One Hero braces on a solid pier with hand outstretched to catch the others
A fourth waits further back on the intact section
ART-CH04-002.atmosphere: Vertigo and strain; the world coming apart under their feet.
avoid: Not a stone bridge melee and not cavern ledges over a chasm: this is an arched aqueduct in open air
No monsters
Do not depict dimensions or jump distances
No lettering on any stones

ART-CH05-002.identity: The reaction and melee rules of Heraldry Skirmish, imagined as a desperate fight against undead soldiers of the Ashlands.
ART-CH05-002.composition: Narrow stone bridge seen from a low three-quarter angle; the clash at centre, shield against shield. Ranks of undead recede into fog behind, the river far below.
details: Narrow humped stone bridge with a cracked parapet and a missing section of coping
Undead soldiers in rusted helms, tattered surcoats and corroded mail, shields pocked and splintered
Adventurers in mismatched gear locking shields, one bracing a spear
One hero falling back wounded, supported by a comrade, dropped weapon at their feet
Fog bank swallowing the far end with more helmets and spear points
Dark river far below with a few bleak reeds
Broken arrows stuck in the bridge deck
activity: Three adventurers hold the line shield-to-shield
A wounded hero staggers back, clutching their side
Undead soldiers push forward in a disciplined rank, faces hollow
avoid: Do not show parties facing across a valley or an aqueduct climb
No gore or dismemberment
No skeleton cartoons or named boss: the undead are soldiers
No lettering on shields

ART-CH06-002.identity: Party creation and the Town Phase, imagined as a crowded hiring hall in a Bastion where adventurers bargain over contracts.
ART-CH06-002.composition: Interior wide shot of a timbered hall; a contract nailed to a post at the focal centre, figures grouped around it beneath captured banners, a clerk at one side with a ledger and coin scales.
details: Heavy timber hall with beams, a long bench, a hearth in the back wall and smoke-stained rafters
Captured banners hanging from the rafters, tattered and without legible devices
Contract sheet nailed to a post, seal dangling, no readable writing
Dwarf with braided beard and pack, elf in light armour, ratkin in scavenged scraps with a hunched posture, orc with tusks and heavy shoulders, halfling holding a tankard, human fighter in mail
Clerk behind a counter with a ledger, quill and a pair of coin scales
Stacked barrels, a notice board of pinned papers drawn as blank rectangles
Mud and straw on the floor, a dog or a rat under the bench
activity: Six adventurers of different ancestries cluster around the post, pointing and haggling
Clerk weighs coin on the scales, a hand pressed on the ledger
Others lounge at benches in the background
avoid: Not a private war room: this is a public Bastion hall with many strangers
Do not show readable text on the contract
No Greythorn-specific features
Not rats and not comic

ART-CH07-002.identity: The equipment chapter, imagined as a Deepwarden forge cut into the rock, the best forges in the surviving world.
ART-CH07-002.composition: Interior of a carved rock forge; the smith at the focal centre quenching a glowing blade in a trough, steam rising; racks of finished mail, helms and axes framing both sides.
details: Rough-hewn rock walls with tool marks and a chimney flue disappearing into the ceiling
Massive anvil, bellows, quench trough and tongs
Blade shown as a bright blank-paper shape with steam in fine lines
Racks of mail shirts, helms and axes along both walls
Smith in a leather apron with heavy forearms, a dwarf in a plain coif
Apprentice working the bellows at one side
Hanging lanterns and an ingot stack, coal bin and sparks as stippling
activity: Smith lowers a blade into the trough
Apprentice leans on the bellows handle
No other figures
ART-CH07-002.atmosphere: Hard, honest labour in a stone-bound city.
avoid: Not the Armoury (stronghold) - this is a master forge in Deepwarden
No fire glow effects, show fire with ink and blank paper
No readable maker's marks
Do not turn the Deepwarden bastion portrait into this - interior only

ART-CH08-002.identity: The magic chapter, imagined as a lone caster in the burned shell of an academy library, the arcane inheritance of broken empires.
ART-CH08-002.composition: Tall broken shelves frame a single figure at night; pages and embers swirl upward around them as a ring of force flares from an outstretched hand.
details: Gutted gothic library hall with charred shelves rising out of frame and a roofless vault with stars through gaps
Burnt codices and scraps of paper whirling in a spiral, pages blank or with illegible scribble only
Ring of force drawn as concentric thin ink rings and radiating short lines from the hand
Caster in a scorched robe, hood back, staff or book at the belt
Collapsed ladder and fallen bookstands on the floor
Ash and ember stippling
A statue or bust with a broken face on a plinth
activity: The caster stands braced, arm outstretched, robes whipped upward by the rising pages
No one else present
ART-CH08-002.atmosphere: Solitary, perilous, wonder tinged with ruin.
avoid: No readable script on the pages
Not the Fallen Observatory scenario (this is a library, not a dome)
No colour or glow effects; line and solid black only
Do not show a specific spell mechanic
sources: 1.3.4 Magic in the Dying Lands (Arcane Spells)

ART-CH09-002.identity: The Bestiary chapter, imagined as the aftermath of a hunt at the edge of the Greenmark, with a slain beast too large to drag home.
ART-CH09-002.composition: Carcass sprawled across the foreground, party standing in the middle ground, dark treeline behind with glinting eyes.
details: Huge slain dire bear seen only in part - a shaggy flank, a slumped head and a great clawed paw - half covered by a cast net, too large to drag home
Spears and a broken net rope across the carcass
Crows landing and clustering on the carcass
Hunters with boar spears, hooded cloaks, a hand-axe, a lantern, one wiping a blade
Forest edge of tall oaks and undergrowth drawn as dense black hatching
Several pairs of small eyes glinting in the dark treeline
Trampled grass and a fallen bow
activity: Party of four stands over the beast in the middle ground, one kneeling to measure it, one scanning the treeline
Crows mob the carcass
avoid: Not the Hunt the Wild Beast scenario, the Giant Tarantula or the Broodmother; the bear is a partial carcass, never a portrait
No gore close-up; carcass drawn with restraint
No visible creatures in the treeline: only tiny eye dots
Not a trophy-pose heroic image

ART-CH10-002.identity: The Scenarios chapter, imagined as a party at a ruined crossroads choosing which of the six climates to enter.
ART-CH10-002.composition: Waystone at the centre; six roads fan out from the crossroads toward six distant landscapes along the horizon, each distinguishable in miniature.
details: Weathered carved waystone with worn pictographs that read as shapes, not letters
Six roads, each with a different surface: root-split flagstones, soot-black pavement, a gaping cave road, snow-edged track, sand-drifted road, plank causeway
Horizon vignettes: forest line, ruined city skyline, cave mouths in mountains, ice-locked towers, dunes and tomb-teeth, fen with stilts
A gibbet or broken signpost stub and a milestone
Small party gathered close to the stone, one tracing its carving with a gloved finger
Dark clouds ruled lightly across the sky
Dried grass and thistle around the junction
activity: Four Heroes cluster at the waystone, reading and pointing down different roads
No other figures
ART-CH10-002.atmosphere: Choice and foreboding at the edge of the known.
avoid: No mountain-spine panorama and no mountain-pass vista
Do not letter the stone
No dragons and no detailed landscapes: the six stay small and simple

ART-CH11-002.identity: The Campaign chapter, imagined as a battered party returning to its Stronghold at dusk after an expedition.
ART-CH11-002.composition: Gate at right; a procession advances along a muddy track from the left toward a palisade gate, fen lanterns as focal points, watchers on the wall above.
details: Palisade of sharpened timbers with a gatehouse and a small tower, ditch with spikes in front
Muddy rutted track with puddles reflecting lantern light
Lantern carried on a pole, hooked lantern hanging at the gate, as areas of untouched paper amid dense hatching
Litter made of two poles and a cloak carrying a wounded Hero
Reed clumps and a fen mist drawn sparsely
Watchers on the wall with torches and spears, silhouetted
Salvaged stonework patched into the palisade base
activity: Four to six figures trudge in single file, two carrying the litter
One watcher on the wall raises a hand
Gate half open

No construction scene and no scaffolding
No monster in view
No glowing lantern rays

ART-WOR-1-2-THE-GRIM-WORLD.identity: The Grim World: kings, bishops and warlords raise banners over land they can barely hold, and peasants bear the cost.
ART-WOR-1-2-THE-GRIM-WORLD.composition: Mid-distance view of a burnt farmstead yard with two warlords' banners planted on opposite sides; the tax cart and armed men fill the yard while a peasant family flees down a lane to one side.
details: Blackened timber farmhouse with a fallen roof and a standing chimney
Two tall banner poles on either side of the yard with tattered banners of different cut (no legible devices)
Tax collector's cart with strongbox, ledger and a seated clerk
Armed men in mismatched gear holding spears, one counting sacks
Burnt barn, scattered tools and a dead cow or ox
Fleeing peasant family on the lane with bundles, a child carried, a dog
Distant smoke column and trampled fields

The family flees down the lane, looking back
Clerk records the taking
ART-WOR-1-2-THE-GRIM-WORLD.atmosphere: Bitter, mundane cruelty of petty war.
avoid: No monsters; the cruelty here is human
Do not show violence against the family
No readable heraldry on banners
Not an abandoned monster-held village street

ART-WOR-1-3-1-THE-FALL.identity: The Fall, the unexplained end of the old empire: no one agrees what caused it, but the ruins of imperial power litter the land.
ART-WOR-1-3-1-THE-FALL.composition: The colossal broken head of an imperial statue half-buried in a ploughed field fills the middle ground, with a farmer and ox tiny beside it.
details: Giant stone head with a crowned brow, one cracked eye socket and half the face sunk in earth
Ploughed furrows curving around the head
Moss and crow-perched weeds on the cracks
Broken statue hand or sandal fragment elsewhere in the field
Distant ridge with a ruined colonnade
Low overcast sky with thin ruled strokes
Farmer's plough and a single ox, a crow on the ear

No other figures

Do not suggest the cause of the Fall (no fire, no sky tear)

ART-WOR-1-3-2-THE-SIX-CLIMATES-OF-RUIN.identity: The shape of the Dying Lands: broken mountains down the spine, the dead empire in the east, the great forest in the west, ice in the north, dunes in the south and swamps in the south-east.
ART-WOR-1-3-2-THE-SIX-CLIMATES-OF-RUIN.composition: A sweeping panorama from the spine of the broken mountains with all six climates under one sky: forest to the west, dead city to the east, ice to the north, dunes to the south and drowned fen to the south-east, with dark cavern mouths in the mountainside below; a lone surveyor with a staff stands in the foreground.
details: Jagged mountain crest with a cairn and a rock ledge foreground
Western forest as dense hatched mass running to a pale coast
Eastern city skyline of snapped towers and domes in fine lines
Northern ice fields with glacial walls and thin hatching
Southern dunes with tomb-teeth along the horizon
South-eastern fen of reeds, black pools and drowned trees in sparse fine lines
Dark cavern mouths and old mine adits in the mountain flank below the ledge (the Undermarches)
Imperial roads as straight lines radiating from the east across the lands
Surveyor with a staff, a rolled map and a leather satchel

avoid: Not a mountain-pass vista with a party and a single road toward one city
No dragons or creatures
No map lettering
No hard compass-rose graphic

ART-CLI-THE-GREENMARK.identity: The Greenmark, the great temperate forest of the surviving world, larger than the maps, where roots take roads and the forest does not recognize human law.
ART-CLI-THE-GREENMARK.composition: A forest road at ground level in deep woods, roots lifting the paving, trees seeming to lean in; a moss-warm grove circle opens in the middle distance.

Road slabs broken and swallowed by roots, a milestone half-buried and tilted
Foresters' warning signs cut in bark as slashes and notches, not letters
Upright hound-like shapes between trunks, dark and indistinct
Grove-circle of standing mossy stones with low mist and a patch of bare paper where snow has melted
Fern, bracken, fallen logs, toadstools
Light shafts as blank paper between trunks

avoid: No people; the climate is the subject

Do not detail the hound shapes: barely seen silhouettes only
No letters in the bark signs

ART-CLI-THE-ASHLANDS.identity: The Ashlands, the cities of the old empires after fire, law and death finished with them, where the city still knows how to count.
ART-CLI-THE-ASHLANDS.composition: Street-level one-point perspective down a soot-black avenue between collapsed forums and leaning temples, with a lit shrine lamp in the near corner.

Shrine niche with a small lit lamp and no worshippers

ART-CLI-THE-UNDERMARCHES.identity: The Undermarches, the endless underworld beneath every foundation, deepest under the broken mountains, where deep elves keep their own law.
ART-CLI-THE-UNDERMARCHES.composition: A cutaway view: a mine shaft or cellar above breaking through into a smooth round tunnel no pick made; a small surveyor with a lantern and an inconsistent map stands at the join.

Stalactites, dripping water and a sour pool
Distant tunnel mouth with a faint far-off lamp
Cracked support beam and loose rubble

No deep elves visible
No glowing crystals
No readable map lettering

ART-CLI-THE-PALE-CITY.identity: The Pale City, the ice-locked northern cities where winter has become government and Hearthhold sends parties north with oil and fire-charms.
ART-CLI-THE-PALE-CITY.composition: View from the northern road toward an ice-locked city gate frozen mid-closing, a small tribute cairn left at the road in the foreground.

No dragons
No glow or aurora

ART-CLI-THE-SUN-DROWNED.identity: The Sun-Drowned, the southern dunes that have climbed over the richest realms, dotted with tomb-cities, salt flats and unburied dead.
ART-CLI-THE-SUN-DROWNED.composition: Wide shot across a dune sea toward tomb-cities breaking the horizon like teeth; a half-uncovered enthroned corpse in the foreground, salt flats glittering where a harbour stood.
details: Tomb-city pyramids and spires jutting from the horizon
Salt flat with stranded ship ribs where a harbour once stood

A few Saltspire guides and travellers in head-wraps leading pack animals (mules)
Bleached bones and broken statuary

ART-CLI-THE-MIRE.identity: The Mire, the southeastern swamps where rivers give out, where bogs swallowed roads and the dead drift below the walkways.
ART-CLI-THE-MIRE.composition: Water-level view along a plank walkway through a drowned village; mangroves grow through the roofs of stilt-houses, pale shapes drift beneath the surface.
details: Leaning stilt-houses over dark water
Mangrove roots bursting through a roof
Plank walkway with missing boards
Water that looks shallow but opens in a darker circle
Pale drifting shapes beneath the surface (faces, hands) in fine lines

A lantern on a pole, unlit

avoid: Not Reedmarch itself (no barges, council hall or toll bridges) and not Vossegar's cathedral

No lettering
Not the Blighted Heartwood or Titan fen scenes

ART-WOR-1-3-3-THE-SIX-BASTIONS.identity: The six Bastions survived the Fall by closing the gate while neighbours screamed outside.
ART-WOR-1-3-3-THE-SIX-BASTIONS.composition: A great Bastion gate grinding shut at dusk, seen from the outside looking in at a low angle; guards strain at the windlass within while desperate figures reach for the closing gap.

ART-BAS-SABLEKEEP.identity: Sablekeep, a fortified chapel-town built into the throat of a ruined imperial city where the Ashlands meet the eastern forest, ruled by the Sable Watch, which survives by burning.

ART-BAS-HEARTHHOLD.identity: Hearthhold, a walled town in the high north built around the Great Hearth that has burned unbroken since the Fall; the smallest, poorest and bravest Bastion.

ART-BAS-SALTSPIRE.identity: Saltspire, a tower-city built around a deep sacred well at the centre of an oasis ringed by salt-pans and the bones of older cities; wealthy and hated.
ART-BAS-SALTSPIRE.composition: Distant approach across salt-pans toward a cluster of tall towers around the oasis; caravans in the foreground, the sacred well-head at the heart.
